chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Is'haq ibn Abd al-Aziz Abu al-Saffatij, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: 'Indeed God took Ibrahim as a servant before He took him as a Prophet, and took him as a Prophet before He took him as a Messenger, and took him as a Messenger before He took him as a friend (Khalil), and took him as a friend before He took him as an Imam.

So when He gathered all these things for him and took his hand, He said to him: O Ibrahim, I am making you an Imam for the people. So great was it in the eyes of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he said: O my Lord, and from my offspring? He said: My covenant shall not be attained by the wrongdoers.

key_terms.إِمَام: Imam — the divinely appointed leader and guide of humanity; here presented as the apex of spiritual stations
key_terms.الظَّالِمِين: The wrongdoers/oppressors — those who have committed injustice, even once, are excluded from the Imamate
key_terms.خَلِيل: Intimate friend (Khalil) — a title specifically given to Ibrahim in Quran 4:125, denoting the highest love of God
key_terms.رَسُول: Messenger (Rasul) — one sent with a divine message and mission to humanity
key_terms.عَبْد: Servant/slave of God — the foundational station of spiritual submission and worship
key_terms.عَهْد: Covenant/pledge of God — the divine appointment of Imamate, restricted to the infallible
key_terms.نَبِيّ: Prophet (Nabi) — one who receives divine inspiration and news from God

ai.seo_question: What are the five spiritual stations of Prophet Ibrahim according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Baqir (AS), establishes the hierarchical spiritual ascent of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) through five divinely conferred stations: servitude, prophethood, messengership, divine friendship (khullah), and finally Imamate — presented as the culminating and most exalted rank. The hadith directly cites Quran 2:124, where God appoints Ibrahim as Imam for mankind, emphasizing that this supreme covenant is withheld from the unjust. In the Shia theological tradition, this hadith is foundational for the doctrine that Imamate surpasses prophethood in spiritual rank, and that Imams must be infallible ('ismah) since no wrongdoer can attain the divine covenant.
